    Simulate a discrete-time SIR or SEIR epidemic

    Source: R/outbreak-compartmental.R
    epi_simulate.Rd

    Uses mass-action transmission with per-step infection probability 1 - exp(-beta * I / N * dt). Progression and recovery similarly use exponential transition probabilities. Transitions use the start-of-step state, and there are no births, deaths, imports, or interventions. Deterministic transitions use expected counts; stochastic transitions use independent binomial draws. Supply rates per time unit; dt sets step length. Set a seed before stochastic runs for reproducibility.

    Usage

    epi_simulate(
  .data,
  beta,
  gamma,
  sigma = NULL,
  steps = 100L,
  dt = 1,
  model = c("sir", "seir"),
  stochastic = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A one-row data frame containing numeric S, I, R, and for SEIR, E compartment counts.

    beta

    Non-negative transmission rate.

    gamma

    Non-negative recovery rate.

    sigma

    Non-negative progression rate, required for SEIR.

    steps

    Number of discrete time steps.

    dt

    Positive time step.

    model

    Either "sir" or "seir".

    stochastic

    Whether to sample transitions rather than take expectations.

    Value

    A tibble with time and compartment columns, including initial state.

    Examples

    epi_simulate(data.frame(S = 999, I = 1, R = 0), beta = 0.3, gamma = 0.1, steps = 10)
#> # A tibble: 11 × 4
#>     time     S     I      R
#>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1     0  999   1    0     
#>  2     1  999.  1.20 0.0952
#>  3     2  998.  1.45 0.210 
#>  4     3  998.  1.75 0.348 
#>  5     4  997.  2.10 0.514 
#>  6     5  997.  2.53 0.714 
#>  7     6  996.  3.05 0.955 
#>  8     7  995.  3.67 1.25  
#>  9     8  994.  4.41 1.59  
#> 10     9  993.  5.31 2.01  
#> 11    10  991.  6.38 2.52
